shortDescription: Nordic forward power prices rose to their highest levels in more than a week on Tuesday, tracking a rise in European gas markets.

children: Nordic forward power prices rose to their highest levels in more than a week on Tuesday, tracking a rise in European gas markets.
Nordic front-quarter baseload power contract (NSBLQc1) rose €1.59, or 1.77%, to €91.25 per megawatt hour (MWh) at 0928 GMT, its highest since August 21.
Nordic front-year (NSBLYc1) gained €0.4, or 0.7%, to €57.3 per megawatt hour.
"I think TTF gas prices continuing up is the main reason today," for the rise in Nordic prices, said LSEG power analyst Ole Djupskaas.

Benchmark Dutch and British wholesale gas prices rose after the first exchange of direct attacks between the United States and Iran in a month renewed fears about even more prolonged supply disruption.
Nordic water reserves available 15 days ahead (PCAEC00) were seen at 10.59 terawatt hours (TWh) below normal, versus 10.70 TWh below normal on Monday.

"Rising pressure over the southern parts of the continent will push low-pressure activity to northwestern and northern Europe. The resulting weather will be mostly dry and sunny until Monday in the south of Central Europe," said LSEG meteorologist Georg Muller.
"Next week will likely be more unsettled and cooler in the southern parts too with temperatures dropping to near or only slightly above normal values," Muller said.
Germany's  year-ahead power (TRDEBYc1), Europe's benchmark contract, slipped €0.1, or 0.09% to €116.9 MWh
